entities.summary: The Starry Night is a seminal post-Impressionist painting by Vincent van Gogh, created circa 1889. This work of art is a masterful representation of the artist's struggles with mental illness and his innovative use of color and brushwork. The painting's bold, swirling clouds and stars against a deep blue background have become iconic in modern art history. It was created during a period of great turmoil in Van Gogh's life, including his hospitalization for mental illness and his struggles with poverty and loneliness. The Starry Night has had a profound impact on modern art, influencing generations of artists and art movements. It is widely regarded as one of the most famous and influential paintings in the history of art. The painting's vivid, expressive style and its use of bold, expressive brushstrokes have made it a beloved and enduring work of art. The Starry Night has also been the subject of numerous exhibitions, books, and documentaries, cementing its place in popular culture. Van Gogh's innovative use of color and his emphasis on capturing the emotional and psychological depths of his subjects have made The Starry Night a timeless classic of modern art.
